ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus nagalandensis* is a medium-sized gecko with a snout-vent length of 75–80 mm. It features a brownish body with dark transverse bands and distinct, strongly keeled tubercles along its flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus nagalandensis* is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of 4–5 distinct, dark brown transverse bands that remain clearly defined against a pale background.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus nagalandensis* inhabits the subtropical broadleaf forests of Nagaland, India, typically found at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 1,500 meters above sea level.
ai.behavior: *Cyrtodactylus nagalandensis* is a strictly nocturnal gecko that remains inactive in rock crevices during the day to avoid predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus nagalandensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus nagalandensis* is endemic to the state of Nagaland in Northeast India, where it inhabits mid-elevation forests at approximately 1,200 to 1,500 meters.
